Help

GroupToDo keeps your tasks, projects and notes as plain markdown files in folders you already own. Everything here is read from those files, and everything you change is written straight back to them. The name is a nod to GTD, the method underneath it.

Getting around

  • The sidebar lists the places you go every day. Hide it with ⇤ at its top, or press \. Bring it back with ☰.
  • Your page opens when you click GroupToDo at the top left. Set your picture there, keep notes about yourself, and see everything in every space that links to you.
  • Back and forward work everywhere, including after you open a page. Use the arrows at the top, or Alt+← and Alt+→.
  • The capture box adds a task to today's page from anywhere. Press N to jump to it. Names, contexts and dates are picked up as you type.
  • Search finds tasks and pages. Paste a path someone copied for you and it opens that page.
  • Where it is saved is the line at the bottom of the sidebar. Click it for folders, the vault file and sync.

Spaces

  • Each space is its own folder, shared with the people in it. The squares at the top right show which spaces are on.
  • Tick any combination. Every view then shows exactly those spaces, and each item carries a coloured tag for its space while more than one is showing.
  • Click a space's name to make it the one new things land in.

Today

  • At the top is what is due today or late, then the next seven days, then your journal for each space, such as Your Work journal.
  • Click a section's title or its arrow to fold it away. Click again to open it.
  • Click the bullet in front of a section, or in front of any line, to focus on it. Everything else leaves the screen and only the trail above it stays. Click a step in the trail to go back out.
  • On a wide screen the journals sit side by side, one column per space.
  • History, next to the date, scrolls back through everything that happened, day by day.

Writing on a line

  • Click a line and type. A menu opens right under the line to set its state, due date, context, person, organisation, project and repeat. Each item shows its key.
  • As you type a name you have used before, it is offered. Tab takes it and turns it into a link. A name written out in full is linked by itself when you leave the line.
  • Dates work the same way: type tomorrow, friday, next week or in 3 days and press Tab. On a task, a date at the end of the line becomes its due date when you leave the line.
  • @, @@, # and [[ list people, contexts, projects and every page.
  • When a line becomes Waiting, the menu asks who you are waiting on.

Keys on a line

KeyDoes
Alt+TMake it a task, or back to a note
Alt+1Make it a project, and link the line to it
Ctrl+EnterNext state: to do, doing, waiting, done, note
Alt+D C P O J RDue, context, person, organisation, project, repeat
TabTake the suggestion, or indent
Shift+TabOutdent
Alt+Shift+↑ ↓Move the line, children and all
↑ ↓ Enter EscIn an open menu: choose, pick, close
Alt+SMove the line to another space

Other keys

KeyDoes
NAdd a task
/Search
\Hide or show the sidebar
?Open this help
TToday
@@Where are you now? Pick a context
g n · g w · g pNext, Waiting for, Projects
g c · g rChat, Weekly review
v b · v t · v rNext as a board, Timeline, Report
v g · v mMind map, Graph
Ctrl+ZUndo the last delete or move
EscClose a panel, menu or this help

Projects

  • A project's status is the folder its file sits in: Cancelled, Active, Someday/Maybe, Waiting for and Completed. Drag a card on the board to move it, and every link to it follows.
  • A project whose open next actions are all waiting on somebody shows as Waiting for, marked “auto”.
  • The timeline shows the plan ahead. Drag a bar to reschedule it.
  • The report shows what got done. Pick a week, month, quarter, half year, year or your own dates, then Copy as text for a status mail.

People and organisations

  • On the People board, drop a person on a project to involve them, or on a next action to hand it over. It then shows in your Waiting for.
  • Organisations work the same way, on projects.
  • People outside the space get a check-in sheet when you ask them for an update.

Weekly review

  • A handful of steps, about fifteen minutes. Everything the app thinks is worth a look is listed there too.
  • The projects step is played as solitaire: one project at a time, stalest first. Every field shows its options from the project's own space. Click one, or drag the card onto it.
